subject: Re: Private deployment - VPC & air-gap constraints (Recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Smith <lauren.smith@avahealth.com>, Devon Park <devon.park@avahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@avahealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment - VPC & air-gap constraints (Recap + next steps)

Hi Lauren / Devon —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to capture concrete next steps. I tried to keep this focused on the technical constraints you described and what we’ll deliver for the Private/VPC deployment evaluation.

Summary of pain points and constraints you raised:
- Strict egress policy: production hosts cannot initiate arbitrary outbound traffic; only allow to approved destinations.
- Air-gapped requirement for certain PHI workloads (gov-like segmentation) — desire to run inference with no direct internet egress for model runtime.
- Data residency: all data and audit logs must remain in US-East (single-region requirement for this initial pilot).
- Limited inbound ports: corporate policy permits only a small set of inbound exceptions; preference for customer-initiated connections/peered control-plane.
- KMS/HSM integration: keys must live in your KMS (AWS KMS / CloudHSM) and we must demonstrate key access patterns and audit events.
- Authentication & SSO: SAML/SCIM support required for provisioning and RBAC.
- Procurement timeline: legal needs standard SLAs and SOC2 evidence; procurement target is mid-August.

What we propose / technical approach (high-level):
- Private deployment model: Redwood ships a customer-managed runtime that can run in your VPC (AMI / EKS helm chart) with control-plane endpoints restricted to outbound-only connections from your VPC to our management endpoints, or via an optional air-gap bundle for fully isolated on-prem installs.
- Networking: For the VPC model we expect to require outbound HTTPS (443) to a small set of FQDNs (control-plane.redwood-inference.com and artifacts.redwood-inference.com). If an outbound proxy is required, we can operate through your proxy (we’ll provide FQDN allowlist + certificate pinning guidance).
- Air-gap option: we can provide an offline install package and allowlist-free runtime; this requires a weekly signed package transfer process (SFTP / physical media) and an on-prem control plane stub for metrics.
- Key management: integration with customer KMS via an agent that never exports plaintext keys; we will provide an HSM interface specification for your infosec review.
- Auditing: we can retain audit logs in your S3 bucket (US-East) or push to your SIEM over a customer-managed endpoint.

Immediate next steps and owners:
1) Diego: deliver a short VPC/networking checklist + template network diagram by EOD Wed (attachment).
2) Marissa (SE): schedule a 90-min technical deep-dive (runbook + test plan) with your infra team — target week of Aug 2.
3) Lauren / Devon: share the procurement contact for contract redlines and your SOC2 evidence portal link.
4) Procurement: send any standard security questionnaire (SIG/SharedAssessments) so we can start pre-filling.

Deliverables attached to this thread:
- redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (networking checklist template)
- avahealth-network-diagram-placeholder.png (editable diagram — please replace subnets/CIDRs)

Questions / clarifications:
- For the air-gap option, can you confirm whether AWS GovCloud (US-Gov) is necessary for the pilot, or if standard US-East accounts with strict egress policies will suffice?
- Can we get a named contact for your security reviewer to set up a short session (30–45m)?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites once Marissa is free.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Diego —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- We do require GovCloud only for federal workloads; for the first pilot (non-federal PHI), US-East with strict egress restrictions is fine.
- For the air-gap option: we would like to see the exact offline package steps and the signing process you mentioned before committing to that approach. That should include how runtime updates are validated.
- Procurement: forwarding our procurement lead (procurement@avahealth.com) to get the contract cadence started. We are targeting an internal approval window of Aug 16–20.

Action items from us:
- Devon: send the network team contact for the allowlist exercise (they’re on vacation today; will provide Monday).
- Procurement: expect SOC2 artifacts link and initial redlines next week.

Please include Marissa on the SE deep-dive invite. We’ll aim for Aug 3 or 4 for the technical session.

Thanks,
Lauren Smith
Head of Data Platforms
